data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 splits resilience by failure class (administrative logic error vs environmental correlation), but it never supplies the distinguishing evidence the problem requires for the 'environmental' case. It states decentralized nodes 'often share the same underlying physical infrastructure' and are therefore more susceptible to external correlated failures, yet offers no causal mechanism or evidentiary test for identifying when geographically/infrastructure-shared nodes are truly coupled by a physical trigger versus merely appearing uncorrelated. The countercondition that the network is infrastructure-diverse is listed as an observation, but the claim and mechanism don't derive how to detect the residual shared cause once obvious co-location is removed—leaving the central distinguishing-evidence demand unmet.
